Subject: Post-call technical deep-dive recap — latency & throughput SLOs

Emily / team — thanks for the deep-dive earlier this morning. Below is a concise technical recap with SLO/throughput targets, model options, and a recommended deployment topology. I’ve attached a short technical brief and a topology diagram for reference.

Summary of what we heard:
- Typical conversational flows: ~2–3 turns, average response ~80–150 tokens.
- Peak concurrency observed (historical): ~180 concurrent chat sessions during peak windows; peak sustained rate ~350 requests/minute (≈6 r/s) with spikes to 1200 r/min (20 r/s) during campaigns.
- Max acceptable latency (biz ask): interactive feel — p95 <= 200 ms for short responses (~100 tokens). p99 <= 450 ms acceptable for up to 256 tokens.

Recommended SLOs (proposal):
- SLO-UI: p95 latency <= 200 ms for generation requests with response <= 128 tokens.
- SLO-TAIL: p99 latency <= 450 ms for generation <= 256 tokens.
- Availability: 99.95% per-month for the inference path (exclude planned maintenance windows).
- Throughput: support sustained baseline 7 r/s with headroom to 25 r/s per region during bursts (autoscale target).

Model & inference requirements:
- Primary model candidate: open LLM family (13B class) quantized to q4_0 or int8 for cost/latency tradeoffs. We recommend testing both 13B and 7B variants in your workload for quality/latency.
- KV cache for chat sessions to avoid re-encoding long histories; prefix caching for template responses.
- Response truncation & streaming enabled for UX-sensitive flows.
- Tokenization: measure 99th-percentile input length; recommend request-side truncation to 512 input tokens for latency-sensitive endpoints.

Deployment topology (recommended):
- Private Dedicated pool in us-west-2 (two AZs) for production-critical traffic with autoscale policies tuned to maintain p95 target.
- Canary lane: route 5–10% traffic to a smaller 7B model pool for cost testing and fallback.
- Cross-region read-only fallback to us-west-1 (warm standby) for failover; automated DNS + model variant fallback policy.
- Network: customer VPC peering with private control plane, encrypted in transit, optional HSM/KMS for key management. See attached network-topology-diagram.png.

Operational controls & mitigations:
- Graceful degradation: on overload, reduce model size automatically (13B -> 7B), enable response sampling, and return cached templates for non-critical flows.
- Autoscale trigger: CPU/GPU utilization + queue latency at 75th percentile.
- Observability: per-route latency, token-cost breakdown, and token-level tracing hooks; we'll provide dashboards and alerting for SLO drift.

Attachments:
- redwood-technical-deep-dive.pdf (detailed perf/cost breakdown)
- network-topology-diagram.png

Action items / next steps:
1) ACME to return the completed SLO questionnaire (Laura has offered to coordinate with Raj).
2) Redwood (Marissa) will run a quick projection matrix (cost vs throughput for 7B/13B q4_0/int8) and send by EOD Tuesday.
3) Schedule a short follow-up to review the cost projection and canary plan (30 min).

If these targets look right, Aditya will surface commercial options and committed capacity pricing for Dedicated pools.
